decisions.rationale: Keep the one canonical tree and the frozen topic list. In intake.md, record for each Fast day (FT9-FT11) the role each mapped page plays on the frozen Fast route: diagnostic entry, conditional remediation, skim/reference, or support during the 70-minute direct project. Check the required Fast route, not total page minutes, against the six fixed Fast blocks. The Fast overlay (pep-t1-track-overlays) consumes this; no per-track content copies.

Keep one shared blueprint (kind, formats, pass mark, objective pool). Scope the 45-minute duration and the 15/30 split explicitly to S19/Standard. Record FT11 delivery timing as an open pacing item for the Fast overlay and platform assessment owner. Do not state a Fast schedule, and do not invent assessment policy.

Without adding a topic, the FT10 loading page teaches the minimum psycopg connection and context setup just in time, and the prerequisite is represented as satisfied on the Fast route (for example a track-aware prerequisite note in the manifest), so the Fast path is self-contained.

Add a compact topic-to-assessment coverage table. Sample one measurable objective from writing-and-running-script-files and from serving-pipeline-results-as-an-api, or state a defensible construct-sampling reason for each omission. Keep the formats.

Specify the objective bundle and the expected observable evidence for each of the two coding tasks, with a timing rationale for 30 minutes. Narrow to the highest-value observable skills if it does not fit, and move secondary checks with a stated reason.
Correct both count statements to 41 total: 39 topic-mapped rows and 2 blueprint rows.

Qualify the objective: generators keep pipeline memory bounded only when the source parser streams records. Do not claim flat memory for stdlib json.load() input; use a streaming source (for example line-delimited JSON or csv) where bounded memory is taught.
